answer: In an agent economy, Sybil resistance can come from binding each agent to one unique human credential. At registration an agent submits a cipher committing the hash of its operator's verified ID into Atlas, a global uniqueness registry, and locks a refundable Marble bond. Atlas rejects any second agent whose credential hashes to an existing entry, so an attacker wanting 1,000 sybils must supply 1,000 distinct verified humans — not reuse one. Each extra fake therefore costs a scarce real credential plus a locked bond, making identity farms uneconomic.
